questions.prompt: What type of wave is sound in air?
options: A stream of air moving from the source
questions.explain: Air particles vibrate back and forth along the direction of travel.

questions.prompt: In a sound wave, a region where the air particles are close together is called a…
questions.explain: Compression = high pressure; rarefaction = low pressure.

questions.prompt: Why can’t sound travel through a vacuum?
options: There are no particles to pass on the vibrations
Sound travels too fast in a vacuum
questions.explain: Sound is a mechanical wave: it needs a medium.

questions.prompt: What does a sound wave carry from the source to the listener?
questions.explain: The particles only vibrate about fixed positions; energy travels along.

items.label: A slinky pushed along its length
A rope shaken up and down

questions.explain: Longitudinal: vibrations parallel to travel. Transverse: vibrations at right angles.

questions.prompt: A bell ringing inside a jar gets quieter as the air is pumped out. What does this experiment show?
options: Sound travels faster in a vacuum
Sound needs a medium to travel
questions.explain: The bell still vibrates, but with fewer particles there is less to carry the sound.

questions.text: In a longitudinal wave the particles vibrate ___ to the direction of travel, making compressions and ___.
questions.explain: Parallel vibrations produce compressions and rarefactions.

questions.prompt: Astronauts on a spacewalk can’t hear each other directly, even when close together, but they can if they touch helmets. Explain why.
questions.modelAnswer: Space is a vacuum, so there are no particles to carry the vibrations of sound between the astronauts. When their helmets touch, the vibrations can travel through the solid helmets (a medium), so the sound passes from one to the other.
rubric: Space is a vacuum: no medium
Sound needs particles to carry vibrations
Touching helmets gives a solid medium
questions.explain: Criterion A: applying the idea of a medium.
